item.title: Can Trump really claim the Nvidia CEO’s return? - Podcast
item.description:
Jonathan Yerushalmy and Reged Ahmad cover what many are describing as the extraordinary intervention by Donald Trump before Nvidia decided to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. They look at how the US president is taking credit for Nvidia’s move, why it’s unprecedented and what might have motivated Trump to get involved.

They also discuss Joe Biden’s new book Promise Me, America, his memoir of his time as president. Why are the reviews so scathing – and what does it say about how the former president will be remembered?

Read more:

A timeline of Jensen Huang’s affair scandal, from quitting Nvidia to his return

Nvidia rejoices at Jensen Huang’s second coming as White House takes victory lap

Promise Me, America by Joe Biden review – former president defends his decisions

item.title: One lame duck and two turkeys as Trump plays the hits at Thanksgiving ceremony
item.description:
Levity was in short supply as president, reeling from midterms rout, talked up his achievements – and fixated on White House vanity project

For some, it was his pardoning of the January 6 rioters or the deployment of masked ICE agents. For others, it was Elon Musk’s chainsaw or the demolition of the White House East Wing.

Donald Trump’s second term as US president has been full of moments when people exclaim: this is the last straw! But on Tuesday even he went too far.

item.title: US army to detonate 68 barrels of toxic lead in Iowa on day before Thanksgiving
item.description:
Residents warned to stay indoors amid conflicting information about how far the dust plume could travel

The US Army is set to detonate 68 barrels – five tons – of lead azide at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa on Wednesday morning, after delays and conflicting information about how far the toxic lead dust plume could travel after the explosion.

That controlled blast has been scheduled for 10am ET on Wednesday, the day before the Thanksgiving holiday.
